items.title: What Happens When Everyone Sends Slop?
items.summary: In episode 1029 of the SuperDataScience Podcast, Jon Krohn talks with Dr. Katie Malone, Host of Linear Digressions about what happens when AI slop starts landing in coworkers' inboxes. It is not just one person doing it, and the result is a world where one person's AI slop ends up talking to another person's AI slop. Katie explains why this is especially hard in large organizations, where people rely on the machinery of processes rather than personal relationships to get work where it needs to go, and where injecting AI does not always fit the way those processes actually work.

items.title: Generative AI & LLMs: From GPT to Open Source Models
items.summary: For most of AI's history the focus was analyzing and predicting. Generative AI creates. Here is what changed, and how to choose between proprietary and open source models. Terms covered: - Generative AI: AI that produces text, code, images, summaries and answers on demand - GPT (Generative Pre-trained Transformer): the architecture behind most large language models - Proprietary LLMs: powerful, easy to start with, priced per token, and your data goes to a third-party server - Open Source LLMs: weights you can download, deploy on your own infrastructure and fine-tune, with no per-token cost and no data leaving your environment Most serious deployments need both. Proprietary for speed and access, open source for control, privacy and cost at production scale. — AI Fundamentals Glossary | H2O.ai University Full playlist: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLAWKlIKS-66E Free courses and certifications: https://h2o.ai/university #GenerativeAI #LLM #OpenSourceAI #AIGlossary #H2Oai
items.summary_html:
For most of AI's history the focus was analyzing and predicting. Generative AI creates. Here is what changed, and how to choose between proprietary and open source models.

Terms covered:
- Generative AI: AI that produces text, code, images, summaries and answers on demand
- GPT (Generative Pre-trained Transformer): the architecture behind most large language models
- Proprietary LLMs: powerful, easy to start with, priced per token, and your data goes to a third-party server
- Open Source LLMs: weights you can download, deploy on your own infrastructure and fine-tune, with no per-token cost and no data leaving your environment

Most serious deployments need both. Proprietary for speed and access, open source for control, privacy and cost at production scale.
